items.title: John Budd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [transcript only]
items.q: But he became a friend and he liked me.

ctx.x: Walter Page. He had been with the Kansas City people and preceded Count Basie I believe. But he became a friend and he liked me. And I talked with these fellows and I would say “Walter, when you play with you and a piano and a drummer in a trio, and when you play a tune, you come to the end of eight bars, there’s a turnaround they call it to go back and some little fill in. And at the end of a tune you have a little something they called a turnaround.” And I said “you play, what you hear played that particular…
Was the Condon bunch as wild as the books say?
